description: Software engineering, Ai Applied and UI/UX
summary:
Órbita Rural is a farmer-focused decision-support system developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s “Field Shift” challenge. It combines NASA GPM IMERG precipitation, NASA POWER temperature, and MODIS vegetation observations with crop calendars, soil information, and a FAO-56-based water balance to make agricultural data easier to use.

Farmers in Rio Verde, Jataí, and Silvânia, Brazil, can check field conditions, compare three crop-rotation scenarios, explore a difficult season day by day, and log harvest results. A conversational assistant helps explain the information, while the calculations—not the AI—provide the numbers. The app can also use bundled data when the API is unavailable.

By turning Earth observations into clear indicators of water stress, heat, and soil cover, Órbita Rural supports more informed decisions in a changing climate. It complements local knowledge and agronomists; it does not replace them.
details:
Órbita Rural turns Earth-observation data into practical decision support across the growing season. Farmers create a field profile with its location, crop rotation, planting date, and soil type. The Python engine combines precipitation from NASA GPM IMERG, temperature from NASA POWER, and vegetation observations from MODIS with crop calendars and a FAO-56-based soil-water balance. It presents the results in three stages: Today shows field conditions and stress indicators; Rehearse compares three crop rotations and lets users explore a difficult season day by day; Log summarizes past seasons and records a harvest estimate locally.

The project is designed to make complex data understandable and help farmers consider water stress, heat, and periods without living soil cover before making decisions. An optional conversational assistant explains results, but the numerical indicators come from the engine, not the AI. The browser app can also fall back to pre-generated data when the API is unavailable.

We built the system with Python 3 for the engine and API, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web app. It runs on a regular computer and browser; no specialized hardware is required. The AI assistant can use an OpenRouter model when configured.

Our creative approach treats farm management like a mission: rehearse before planting, monitor during the season, and record results after harvest. We considered local crop calendars, soil-water capacity, data dates, uncertainty, accessibility, and the limits of regional data—the results represent municipalities, not individual plots. The tool is intended to complement farmers’ experience and agronomists’ advice, not replace them.
